panelspatialprobit

Bayesian estimation of panel spatial probit and panel spatial ordered probit models in R.

For unit ii and period tt the latent outcome follows

zt=ρWzt+Xtβ+WXtθ+α+ut,ut=λMut+εt,εt∼N(0,IN),z_t = \rho W z_t + X_t\beta + W X_t\theta + \alpha + u_t,\qquad u_t = \lambda M u_t + \varepsilon_t,\qquad \varepsilon_t \sim N(0, I_N),

with yit=1{zit>0}y_{it} = 1\{z_{it} > 0\} (binary) or yit=jy_{it} = j when κj−1<zit≤κj\kappa_{j-1} < z_{it} \le \kappa_j (ordered). Supported options:

  • Spatial specification: model = "sar", "sdm", "slx", "sem", "sdem", "sarar" or "none", with separate error weights M if needed.
  • Spatial weights: one matrix, or one per period (time-varying weights).
  • Heterogeneity: pooled, random or spatially autocorrelated random effects (effects =). Correlated random effects use Mundlak means (cre = ~ x1) or Chamberlain period values (cre = list(type = "chamberlain", vars = ~ x1)), and time_effects = TRUE adds period dummies.
  • Impacts: average direct, indirect and total effects on probabilities (per category for ordered models), population-averaged or conditional on the random effects, overall or per period.
  • Dynamics: lagged outcomes and their spatial lag, with Wooldridge initial conditions (dynamic = psp_dynamic()), or latent AR(1) dynamics (psp_dynamic(latent = TRUE)), and dynamic response paths (psp_response_path()).
  • Errors: normal (probit) or Student-t (errors = psp_t(df), robit).
  • Missing outcomes are imputed during sampling.
  • Fit and checking: predicted and counterfactual probabilities (predict(newdata = )), hit rate and AUC (psp_classification()), posterior predictive checks (psp_ppc()), and an experimental simulated likelihood with DIC (psp_loglik(), psp_dic()).
  • Sampler: written in C++. Several chains are reproducible from one seed, and convergence diagnostics come from the posterior package.

The package is in early development (see plan/ for the roadmap). Rows must form a balanced panel (outcomes may be missing).

Example 

library(panelspatialprobit)

W <- psp_weights(rook_weights(10, 10), style = "W")
d <- sim_psprobit(W, T = 5, beta = c(0, 1, -1), rho = 0.6, sigma_alpha = 0.8, seed = 42)

fit <- psprobit(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d, index = c("id", "time"), W = W,
                control = psp_control(seed = 1))
summary(fit)          # posterior summary, R-hat, ESS, impacts
psp_impacts(fit)      # direct / indirect / total effects on P(y = 1)
predict(fit)          # posterior mean probabilities, in the row order of `d`

# ordered outcome
d2 <- sim_psprobit(W, T = 5, beta = c(0, 1, -1), rho = 0.5, cutpoints = c(0.8, 1.6), seed = 7)
fit2 <- psoprobit(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d2, index = c("id", "time"), W = W)

How the sampler works

Each model reduces, given its spatial parameters, to a Gaussian kernel ‖Az−b‖2\lVert Az - b\rVert^2 for the latent outcomes with a sparse operator A=(I−λM)(I−ρW)A = (I - \lambda M)(I - \rho W), so one sampler handles every variant. Each iteration draws, in order:

  1. the latent outcomes, with exact, warm-started truncated-normal Gibbs sweeps that update residuals in place (no matrix solves);
  2. ρ\rho, by griddy Gibbs with β\beta integrated out;
  3. β\beta, then λ\lambda (griddy Gibbs), then the random effects and their variance (half-Cauchy prior);
  4. for ordered models, the cut-points: an Albert–Chib step plus a joint move of cut-points and latent values;
  5. a scale move that rescales all of the above jointly (Liu & Sabatti, 2000), which improves mixing.

plan/02_estimation_algorithms.md gives the details.

Validation

  • Reference sampler: the C++ engine is tested against a dense pure-R sampler that uses different algorithms (tests/testthat/test-reference.R).
  • Simulation-based calibration: every supported model variant passes SBC (validation/sbc/run_sbc.R).
  • Monte Carlo study: bias, RMSE and coverage at fixed parameters, including state dependence versus heterogeneity in dynamic models (validation/montecarlo/run_mc.R).
  • Impacts: checked against finite differences of the exact probabilities.
  • Cut-point moves: a stationarity test on a toy ordered model (tests/testthat/test-cutmove.R).
  • Cross-checks: agreement with spatialprobit on the Katrina data and with MCMCpack::MCMCoprobit for non-spatial ordered probit (validation/crosscheck/).

The vignettes vignette("getting-started", package = "panelspatialprobit") and vignette("ordered-outcomes", package = "panelspatialprobit") walk through complete analyses.
